blocks.text: BioReason-Pro[1] 正是为此而生，它融合了多种模态：a) 一个编码序列和结构的蛋白质模型；b) 来自预测蛋白质功能、识别蛋白质家族和功能区域的工具的文本注释。LLM 利用这些信息，用自然语言推理蛋白质可能具有的功能。这种多模态架构的目的，就是针对了解甚少的蛋白质提出有用的假设。

blocks.text: 在最初版本的基础上，我们与 NVIDIA 和 Arc Institute 合作开发了 BioReason-Pro 2，NVIDIA 将以 BioNeMo 开放模型的形式发布。在模型开发过程中，我们的可解释性研究发现了两个问题：模型对文本注释的依赖过重，以及蛋白质嵌入与文本嵌入之间存在尺度不匹配。这些发现促使我们修改了训练输入，让模型的论断建立在具体的蛋白质区域和氨基酸上，并重新调整了蛋白质嵌入的尺度。这些改动共同将已注释序列特征的识别比例从 44% 提升到 84%，并改善了定位能力，能够正确预测 85% 的特征位置，误差在真实位置五个氨基酸以内。

inlines.text: 加强 BioReason-Pro 对蛋白质的理解

blocks.text: 最初的 BioReason-Pro（BR-Pro）以多种形式接收蛋白质信息。一个名为 ESM3[2] 的专用模型将序列和可用的结构转换为每个氨基酸残基的数值表示（即嵌入），再通过一个学习得到的适配器[3] 让语言模型能够使用这些信息。

blocks.text: 模型还接收了其他工具基于同一序列生成的文本。GO-GPT 预测基因本体（GO）[4]术语，这是描述蛋白质功能的标准词汇；InterPro[5]（IPR）则识别蛋白质家族、结构域（具有特征性结构或功能的区域）以及位点。

blocks.text: ESM3 嵌入、GO-GPT 预测和 InterPro 注释都源自同一条蛋白质序列。最初的 BR-Pro 学到的是在结构域层面描述蛋白质，而这类信息 InterPro 已经以文本形式提供了。把 InterPro 和 GO-GPT 放进提示词后，它无需 ESM3 嵌入就能还原出大部分 GO 术语预测，这与 Fang 等人[6]独立审计的发现一致。此外，如何有效利用非文本输入是一个更普遍的难题：视觉-语言模型在视觉任务上的表现也可能不如对应的纯文本模型（Weng 等[7]，Nikankin 等[8]）。

blocks.text: Proteins carry out much of the work inside cells. Understanding what they do is essential to uncovering disease mechanisms and developing new medicines. Yet the function of many proteins is still unknown, and the experiments that reveal it are slow. AI models that propose specific, testable hypotheses could point those experiments in the right direction.

inlines.text: Proteins carry out much of the work inside cells. Understanding what they do is essential to uncovering disease mechanisms and developing new medicines. Yet the function of many proteins is still unknown, and the experiments that reveal it are slow. AI models that propose specific, testable hypotheses could point those experiments in the right direction.

blocks.text: BioReason-Pro[1] aims to do this by fusing modalities: a) a protein model that encodes sequence and structure and b) text annotations from tools that predict protein functions and identify protein families and functional regions. An LLM uses these to reason in natural language about what the protein might do. The purpose of this multimodal architecture is to surface useful hypotheses about poorly understood proteins.

blocks.text: Generating these hypotheses beyond existing annotations depends on combining protein and text information effectively. In the original BioReason-Pro, text annotations supplied much of the information about functional regions the model learned to describe. We focused on understanding what the protein embeddings contributed to the model’s reasoning and how they shaped its hypotheses.

blocks.text: Building on the original release, we worked with NVIDIA and the Arc Institute to develop BioReason-Pro 2, which NVIDIA is releasing as a BioNeMo open model. During the model development process, our interpretability investigations revealed disproportionate reliance on text annotations and a scale mismatch between protein and text embeddings. These findings led us to revise the training inputs, grounding its claims in specific protein regions and amino acids, and rescale protein embeddings. Together, these changes increased the share of annotated sequence features identified from 44% to 84% and improved localization to correctly predict 85% of the feature locations within five amino acids of their true positions.

blocks.text: BioReason-Pro 2 generated novel hypotheses about the function of two poorly characterized human proteins, SMIM32 and RCDG1*, which we validated in the wet lab. Because wet-lab experiments are slow and costly, deciding which hypotheses to test requires confidence in how the model arrived at them, so we also used interpretability to examine their basis. blocks.text: The original BioReason-Pro (BR-Pro) received protein information in several forms. A specialized model called ESM3[2] converted sequence and available structure into numerical representations, or embeddings, for each amino acid residue, and a learned adapter[3] made these accessible to the language model.

blocks.text: ESM3 embeddings, GO-GPT predictions, and InterPro annotations are all derived from the same protein sequence. The original BR-Pro learned to describe proteins at the domain level, information InterPro already supplied as text. With InterPro and GO-GPT in its prompt, it could recover most of its GO term predictions without ESM3 embeddings, consistent with findings from an independent audit by Fang et al.[6]. Further, making effective use of non-text inputs is a broader challenge: vision–language models can also perform worse on visual tasks than on their text counterparts (Weng et al.[7], Nikankin et al.[8]).

blocks.text: In BioReason-Pro, supervised fine-tuning (SFT) was used to teach the model to write reasoning traces that, step by step, lead to functional predictions. These traces taught the model to link InterPro's domain annotations and GO-GPT's predictions into molecular hypotheses. To make the model more reliant on its protein embeddings, we changed both what the traces build on and how finely they describe the protein.

blocks.text: Sampling hypotheses from the model

inlines.text: Sampling hypotheses from the model

blocks.text: BioReason-Pro 2 is a hypothesis generator. Repeated generations for a protein‡ offer a diversity of explanations, and the best of ten raises the mean judge score from 6.8 to 8.4 and GO recall from 0.70 to 0.82, while reliability more than doubles (Figure 12). Used as a reinforcement learning (RL) reward, LLM-as-a-judge raised a single generation's judge score from 6.8 to 7.6. Used as a reviewer, a frontier LLM can compare a dozen generations and distill the most plausible novel hypotheses for scientists to test. To that end, we are open-sourcing an atlas of 33.5 million BioReason-Pro 2 reasoning traces across over 300,000 proteins.

blocks.text: Interpretability guided both how we built BioReason-Pro 2 and how we tested its hypotheses. Input interventions exposed coarse use of the ESM3 embeddings, which led us to remove InterPro from training and enrich the granularity of protein grounding in the traces. Internal representations also revealed a scale mismatch between protein and text norms, which we fixed by appropriate rescaling.

blocks.text: There is further work to do: BioReason-Pro 2 was trained for a particular format for discussing protein function and struggles to follow requests for other formats; interleaving question-answering traces may help broaden that flexibility.
